l became known as the first openly transgender individual to hold public office in the United States, but withdrew before taking up the role when it was revealed that he had served four months in prison in 2008 on a conviction for identity and credit card fraud and tampering with physical evidence.

Earlier this week, Laughton's defense submitted a memorandum requesting that he be sentenced to just over 17 years in prison for his crimes. 

The memorandum describes Laughton as a "complex 42-year-old woman” and refers to him as an ordained minister who championed civil rights, including transgender rights and championed raising the minimum wage and mental health care for students. 

The memorandum seems to assign most, if not all, of the blame for the sexual offenses against children to Groves, and argues that Laughton should not receive a higher sentence than Groves. 

He also uses Laughton's gender identity, mental health issues and learning disabilities as mitigating factors.

While the defense sentencing memorandum described Laughton as a victim and attempted to place the majority of the blame on Groves, the prosecution strongly disagreed and noted that Laughton admitted to “persuading" Groves to commit the crimes.

“To be clear: Groves was an active participant and is not a victim. She knew that what she was doing was wrong and that, at a minimum, her career would be in danger if they were discovered.
